about: Travis J. Mock, a distinguished counselor and business litigator at Rakower Law PLLC in New York City, New York, brings his keen legal acumen to represent an impressive range of clients, from individuals to global Fortune 500 companies. Leveraging his extensive experience and skill, he has successfully handled cases in both state and federal courts, and efficiently resolved disputes through mediation and arbitration. His impressive portfolio spans various subject areas, including complex commercial litigation, contract disputes, intellectual property, insurance, financial services, employment law, appeals, civil rights, whistleblower litigation and corporate investigations.

Mr. Mock also focuses on compliance monitoring, ERISA executives in transition, commercial lending, fraud litigation, real estate litigation and white collar defense, amongst other areas. Additionally, he has represented numerous high net worth individuals and international institutions, and proven his excellence in trials, arbitrations and regulatory enforcement. Furthermore, his legal abilities include representation of hedge funds, professional liability, partnership disputes and foreign sovereigns as well.

After completing his Bachelor of Arts degree at Dickinson College in 2004, Mr. Mock earned his Juris Doctorate from the University of Virginia School of Law in 2009. While there, he honed his skills as an article editor for the Virginia Journal of International Law. He was admitted to practice law in New York in 2010 and has spent over a decade litigating various global Am Law 100 and boutique litigation firms. He also holds admission before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 2nd and 9th Circuits, the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Iowa.

An upstanding figure in the legal fraternity of New York, Mr. Mock is actively involved in the New York City Bar Association. He presently serves on the New York State Courts of Superior Jurisdiction Committee. He is also a stalwart member of the Federal Bar Council, donning the hat of assistant treasurer and serving on the Editorial Board of the Council's Quarterly journal. Additionally, he holds membership in the Council's Inn of Court.

Mr. Mock exhibits an unwavering commitment to both his community and the arts. As a member of the board of directors for Music on the Inside (MOTI), a non-profit organization, he tirelessly works towards connecting individuals affected by imprisonment with professional musicians to serve as educators and role models. Through music's enchanting and transformative language, his actions instill hope and facilitate healing in youth and adults' hearts.
